entities.summary:
Saint Charalambos (c. 87 CE – 202 CE), Bishop of Magnesia on the Maeander, was a revered early Christian martyr whose steadfast faith under extreme persecution solidified his place as one of the most venerated figures in Eastern Orthodox Christianity. Active during the tumultuous reign of Emperor Septimius Severus, Charalambos's refusal to renounce Christianity, even in his advanced age, became a powerful testament to the nascent religion's resilience against imperial Roman authority. His life and death exemplify the brutal clash between the burgeoning Christian movement and the traditional polytheistic structures of the Roman Empire in Asia Minor, serving as an enduring symbol of spiritual fortitude.

According to hagiographic accounts, Charalambos was arrested in his episcopal city of Magnesia on the Maeander, a prominent city in the Roman province of Asia, around 202 CE. Despite being approximately 113 years old, he endured severe torture, including being flayed alive, during the anti-Christian persecutions orchestrated by the proconsul Lucian and the military commander Lucius. Miraculous events are said to have accompanied his suffering, leading to the conversion of his torturers and even Lucian's daughter, Blandina. These narratives emphasize his unwavering commitment to his faith, even as his body was subjected to extreme brutality, making him a potent figure of spiritual triumph over physical pain.
